rules.statement: The compiled Official Context Package is the single canonical context artifact for a Node. It may include direct informational References for the Node itself, while only the effective normative Parent/local Context is exported to semantic Children.
rules.title: One canonical package with an explicit export boundary
rules.why: Local background information must not become inherited governance, but the local view and normative export must still come from one deterministic authenticated package.

rules.statement: Human context changes are authored in `CONTEXT.src.md`; generated context views, package contents, machine state, and harness adapters are not edited directly.
rules.title: Edit source, not generated output
rules.why: One editable source prevents drift between equivalent outputs.

rules.statement: Framework bookkeeping belongs under `.context/` and should not be required reading for normal human or agent work.
rules.title: Keep compiler bookkeeping out of the normal workflow
rules.why: IDs, snapshots, provenance, and digests are necessary for the compiler but should not dominate the user experience.

rules.statement: A Reference may expose useful Topics and Resources to the current Node, but its Rules never become effective, its Overrides/Removes never alter normative Context, and the Reference relationship is never inherited by Children.
rules.title: References stay informational
rules.why: Related information must not silently become governance merely because it uses the same immutable package infrastructure.

rules.statement: A Node may compose several semantic Parents. Parent order has no precedence; non-orthogonal conflicts must be resolved explicitly.
rules.title: Parents are unordered
rules.why: Orthogonal context commonly meets at one Node; ordering must never hide a contradiction.

rules.statement: Every addressable context element has a stable ID independent of its title, wording, file location, and presentation.
rules.title: Stable identity
rules.why: Children must be able to remove, override, trace, or debug inherited elements even after human wording changes.

rules.statement: Published official contexts expose stable IDs for Rules and other elements that child Nodes may reference.
rules.title: Publish IDs that children may reference
rules.why: Users must be able to discover the correct target without searching hidden comments or machine YAML.

rules.statement: Keep the official entry context compact and use Topics to load deeper context only when needed; Topic targets distinguish Required from Optional material.
rules.title: Keep entry context small
rules.why: Context is scarce working memory and should be spent on information relevant to the current task.

rules.statement: `STATE.md` describes the current local project situation and is never inherited as governance by child Nodes.
rules.title: State stays local
rules.why: Temporary project reality is useful locally but is not a reusable Rule of descendants.

rules.statement: Project code and canonical project context must not depend on a particular LLM or agent harness; harness-specific files are thin generated adapters at the edge.
rules.title: Canonical context is model- and harness-neutral
rules.why: A project should remain portable across models and tools without duplicating its truth.

rules.statement: Prefer Node roots that contain the files they primarily govern; keep the existing directory structure when it already fits.
rules.title: Align Node roots with governed files
rules.why: Humans and agents should encounter the applicable Context naturally from the files they change.

rules.statement: Keep `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` present when they are useful to the repository even when ContextCanon is present.
rules.title: Keep familiar repository documents useful
rules.why: ContextCanon should complement familiar project navigation rather than replace it.

rules.statement: Write technical documentation in precise, plain prose for intelligent readers; introduce unfamiliar concepts before using specialized terms and avoid unexplained internal shorthand, inflated marketing language, and unnecessary jargon.
rules.title: Write for intelligent readers
rules.why: Context should reduce interpretation effort for humans and models rather than create a private vocabulary barrier.

topics.title: Context authoring

topics.title: Context composition

topics.title: Harness adapters
